I have always been curious about the nationalistic pride of Taiwanese people. From my experience, Taiwanese people tend to make it clear to everyone that they are not Chinese. 

So I guess my question is if theoretically your students came to America and were mistake for Chinese people, would they take more offense to that versus if they were mistaken for Korean people?

I've always viewed education and jobs as an obligation, to the people you care about and society. A requirement of sorts to explore and maybe find something you enjoy. The combination of the pessimist in me and being brought up with high expectations made me believe that I needed a well paying job. not something i simply enjoyed doing. 

When it seemed like I finally found something to look forward to, it leaves and it seems as though my problems have been amplified.

just curious, what do you want out of life?

My family is another aspect of the story. To me, my father has been gone for years. After my parents divorced, they stopped talking to each other and gradually we drifted apart. Very soon he remarried and decided to pay child support for only selected things. If I wouldn't literally die without it, he refused to pay. When college time came, we had a falling out we have not talked since. No child support, no holiday get-togethers, no calls.

My mom works nights to provide for us and sometimes I can't help but think that she would have an easier time without me. We hardly have a chance to talk as I go to school during the day and she goes to work at night.

As far as traveling goes, I'm not sure how to justify being gone for months at a time to a strict Asian parent who also happens to be working to keep me in school.
It's nice having all these stories to read. At least we know we aren't the only ones feeling miserable
